newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Pan Am Silver wins 49 pct of Russian mine.
newsitem.headline: Pan Am Silver wins 49 pct of Russian mine.

text.p: Canada's Pan American Silver Corp won a tender for 49 percent of Russia's ailing Dukat silver complex, developer of the former Soviet Union's largest silver mine, Property Fund officials said on Thursday.
The company offered investment worth $302.6 million, well above the minimum offer of $77.7 million.

Pan Am Silver must transfer 20 percent of the sum within one month of signing a formal deal and invest the whole sum before the end of 1999 for modernisation. It must also pay Dukat's debts of over 300 billion roubles over a three-year period.
The tender offered 139.58 million shares at a starting price of 10,000 roubles.

Dukat, based in the northeastern Magadan region, has recoverable reserves of 14,000 tonnes of silver and 30 tonnes of gold, the local geology committee said. It contains about two-thirds of Russia's unmined silver reserves.
The tender replaced an earlier sale, which was cancelled after only one foreign firm reached the final stages of the contest.
